newsitem.title: UK: JGBs offer top returns in March in Salomon index.
newsitem.headline: JGBs offer top returns in March in Salomon index.

text.p: Japanese government bonds, which offer some of the smallest nominal yields in the world, were the only sector of the Salomon Brothers world government bond index to offer positive returns in March, Salomon said on Thursday.
The total index showed losses of 0.70 percent in local currency terms, and 0.53 percent in dollars.

Debt markets have been beset by concerns over the possiblity of rising U.S. inflation and the need for tighter U.S. monetary policy, a concern which was partially realised when the Federal Reserve raised interest rates on March 25.

Also speculation over a delay to the start of European Economic and Monetary Union had damaged some European markets, analysts said. JGBs made gains of 0.50 percent in yen terms and 1.02 percent in dollars, while other sectors included in the index showed losses.

The markets which fared worst were Canadian and French bonds, both of which made losses of 1.50 percent in local currency terms. In U.S. dollar terms, Canadian bonds lost 1.28 percent, while French bonds lost 1.34 percent.

British gilts also put in a weak performance making a loss of 1.48 percent in sterling and 1.55 percent in dollars. Elsewhere in Europe, German Bunds registered a 0.74 percent deficit in marks, while Italian bonds lost 0.50 percent in lira terms. In dollar terms they made losses of 0.57 and 0.69 percent respectively.

Salomon's bond index is calculated using all government bonds with over one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns take account of price moves and accrued interest.
